lines: The economy slows down and the bike shop cuts your hours by a quarter. Your pay drops from 2,400 to 1,800 dollars, a 600 dollar gap. It lasts 6 months, and your 3,600 dollar emergency fund covers it exactly.
The business cycle has four phases. Expansion, when the economy grows. Peak, the top. Contraction, when it shrinks. And trough, the bottom, before growth comes back.
A recession is a big, broad drop that lasts more than a few months. A common rule of thumb is two quarters in a row of shrinking real GDP. Officially, a committee at the NBER decides.
Since 1945, the average expansion has lasted about 5 years, and the average recession about 10 months. The Great Recession lasted 18 months. The 2020 recession lasted just 2.
Leading indicators, like stock prices and building permits, tend to turn first. Lagging indicators, like the unemployment rate, turn last.
In a recession, the Fed usually cuts interest rates to make borrowing cheaper. When the economy runs too hot, it raises them.
You can't control the cycle, but you can prepare. Build your emergency fund in good times. In bad times, lean on it, and keep investing if your job is safe.
Snowshoe hares boom and crash about every 8 to 11 years, and the lynx follow a step behind. The hares that make it through have a safe burrow. Your emergency fund is yours.
